name: Deletion Normal Form for Cover-Recursive Obstructions
statement: Let $O$ be a forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class, let $e$ be a coordinate, orient it by $b$, and put $D=O_e^b\setminus O_e^{1-b}$. Add to the opposite semicube the missing mates $\{(x,1-b):x\in D\}$ to obtain $G$. Then $G$ is a cover-recursively peripheral expansion of $O/e$ along $O_e^b$, coordinate $e$ is peripheral in $G$, and $O$ is recovered by deleting exactly those added vertices, each of which has its $e$-neighbor in $G$.
proof: The completed opposite section is $O_e^{1-b}\cup D=O_e^0\cup O_e^1=O/e$, while the unchanged $b$-section is $O_e^b\subseteq O/e$. Hence $G=((O/e)\times\{1-b\})\cup(O_e^b\times\{b\})$. The base and site are proper pc-minors of $O$, so both belong to the cover-recursive class; their permitted peripheral expansion is $G$. Deleting the newly supplied mates returns $O$.
